front_blocks.md: What is a **sample space** in the context of probability?

back_blocks.md: A **sample space** is the set of **all possible outcomes **of an experiment.
It may be a list or a grid showing all the possible outcomes.

cards.front_md: What is a **sample space** in the context of probability?
cards.back_md:
A **sample space** is the set of **all possible outcomes **of an experiment.

It may be a list or a grid showing all the possible outcomes.

front_blocks.md: You can **always** use a **sample space grid **to represent **all possible outcomes**.

back_blocks.md: When combining **more than two things**, you may need to go back to **listing outcomes** instead of using a grid.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

You can **always** use a **sample space grid **to represent **all possible outcomes**.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

When combining **more than two things**, you may need to go back to **listing outcomes** instead of using a grid.

front_blocks.md: How do you **calculate probabilities** using a **sample space**?

back_blocks.md: **Count** the **possibilities you want**, then **divide** by the **total number of possibilities **in the sample space.
(Note: this only works if every possibility in the sample space is **equally likely**.)

cards.front_md: How do you **calculate probabilities** using a **sample space**?
cards.back_md:

(Note: this only works if every possibility in the sample space is **equally likely**.)
